text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad opened the second Langkawi Motor Show, declaring that Malaysians are not tired of learning, particularly engineering technology which could propel the country to greater heights.
- The Land and Co-operative Development Ministry is investigating reports that some state authorities are defying the directive to suspend acquisition of land for industrial and commercial projects.

- In the short time since the Proton Saga made its debut in 1985, Malaysia has sped from being a mere assembler to manufacturer and exporter of its own vehicles and this year even bought over a foreign automotive engineering company.
- Employees of Kwong Yik Bank Bhd and DCB Bank can rest assured of one thing -- none of them will lose their jobs following the merger of their banks.
- In the privatization exercise being planned for Percetakan Nasional Malaysia Bhd, the government printers should not be sold to just anybody, executive chairman Mohd Yusof Hitam said.
- Telephone subscribers will be able to use a common number for their home, office, hand and car phones under the personalised number system to be introduced next year.
